title: Lifecycle `footer` function captures user's environment - which can result in massive memory explosion
description:
See https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/7804

Here's the scenario

- `case_match()` throws a once-per-session lifecycle warning now
- testthat triggers lifecycle warnings unconditionally, not just once per session
- `lifecycle:::deprecate_warn0` **accidentally captures the user's environment** in the warning condition object's `footer` function field
- If you have many tests that trigger the warning AND your user environment is large, then that can result in an OOM crash of R

I actually recently ran into this myself in furrr but had no idea what the problem was. It resolved itself when I got rid of all the deprecation warnings from purrr so I didn't think too much of it.

I wonder if we can change from `footer` as a condition field to a `cnd_footer()` S3 method, and store the minimal amount of stuff in the condition itself that is required to reproduce this footer message from a `cnd_footer()` S3 method instead. That way we don't accidentally capture large function objects in a lifecycle condition.

``` r
library(dplyr)

tibble(
  x = 1:1000
) |> 
  cross_join(
    tibble(
      y = 1:1000
    )
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    v0 = "y"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    v1 = case_match(v0, "blah" ~ "y")
  )
#> Warning: There was 1 warning in `mutate()`.
#> ℹ In argument: `v1 = case_match(v0, "blah" ~ "y")`.
#> Caused by warning:
#> ! `case_match()` was deprecated in dplyr 1.2.0.
#> ℹ Please use `recode_values()` instead.
#> # A tibble: 1,000,000 × 4
#>        x     y v0    v1   
#>    <int> <int> <chr> <chr>
#>  1     1     1 y     <NA> 
#>  2     1     2 y     <NA> 
#>  3     1     3 y     <NA> 
#>  4     1     4 y     <NA> 
#>  5     1     5 y     <NA> 
#>  6     1     6 y     <NA> 
#>  7     1     7 y     <NA> 
#>  8     1     8 y     <NA> 
#>  9     1     9 y     <NA> 
#> 10     1    10 y     <NA> 
#> # ℹ 999,990 more rows

lobstr::obj_size(
  environment(dplyr:::the$last_warnings[[1]]$cnd$footer)$trace_env[["..."]]
)
#> 24.15 MB

footer_function_captured_in_lifecycle <- dplyr:::the$last_warnings[[1]]$cnd$footer
footer_function_captured_in_lifecycle
#> function (...) 
#> {
#>     footer <- NULL
#>     if (!direct) {
#>         top <- topenv(user_env)
#>         if (is_namespace(top)) {
#>             pkg <- ns_env_name(top)
#>             url <- pkg_url_bug(pkg)
#>             likely_line <- cli::format_inline("The deprecated feature was likely used in the {.pkg {pkg}} package.")
#>             if (is_null(url)) {
#>                 report_line <- "Please report the issue to the authors."
#>             }
#>             else {
#>                 report_line <- cli::format_inline("Please report the issue at {.url {url}}.")
#>             }
#>             footer <- c(footer, i = likely_line, ` ` = report_line)
#>         }
#>     }
#>     if (is_interactive()) {
#>         footer <- c(footer, if (!always) {
#>             cli::col_silver("This warning is displayed once per session.")
#>         }, cli::format_inline(cli::col_silver("Call {.run lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()} to see where this warning was generated.")))
#>     }
#>     footer
#> }
#> <bytecode: 0x10b5087e0>
#> <environment: 0x10b509f20>

# captures everything from the `lifecycle:::deprecate_warn0` frame
names(environment(footer_function_captured_in_lifecycle))
#>  [1] "maybe_push_warning" "wrn"                "trace"             
#>  [4] "footer"             "msg"                "id"                
#>  [7] "always"             "direct"             "call"
```

title: Verbosity is not respected on R6 init calls
description:

When initializing an R6 class that contains a `deprecate_warn` it only throws the message the first time. Both when running with `lifecycle_verbosity` R option and in the `{testthat}` expectation.

### Expected behavior

It should throw the warning on every call if verbosity is set to `warning`

Reproducible code below:

```r
rlang::local_options(lifecycle_verbosity = "warning")
A <- R6::R6Class("A", list(
  initialize = function() {
    lifecycle::deprecate_warn('1.0.0', 'A$new()')
  }
```

title: Provide tool to log signal_stage() signals
Lexically-scoped verbosity
description:
The behaviour for soft-deprecation verbosity in unit tests was originally intented to depend on whether the soft-deprecated function is called from the tested package or downstack:

- If called from the tested package, the default verbosity is set to `"warning"`
- If called from a dependency, it is set to `"quiet"`

This conditional verbosity is implemented in `deprecate_soft()` via the envvar `TESTTHAT_PKG` which is set to the package being tested. Unfortunately, this default stopped working correctly with testthat 3e because it hardcodes verbosity to warning. The problem is that verbosity is currently set via a global option whereas we really want some sort of lexical scoping instead.

I think it's a good idea to let testthat set the lifecycle verbosity, but we need a lexically scoped mechanism. I see two options. The simplest is to allow defining verbosity with a local binding:

```r
local_bindings(
  .lifecycle_verbosity = "warning"
)
```

This is not practical when the deprecation is signalled from helpers though, because the calling environment of these helpers will not have that binding in scope. What we really want is to set verbosity for the whole namespace. So we could provide a custom tool for this:

```r
lifecycle::local_verbosity(
  rlang = "warning",
  purrr = "warning"
)
```

testthat would use this to enable warnings for the package being tested instead of setting the global option.

We could also frame the behaviour with the global environment in terms of this mechanism. You could disable this behaviour like this:

```r
lifecycle::poke_verbosity(global = NULL)
```

This would be less risky than using the global `options(lifecycle_verbosity = "quiet")` which silences all warnings without distinction.

What do you think @hadley?

title: Present tense / past tense mixing
description:
Hi 👋 

I am really enjoying using `lifecycle` 👏 
I have just found an "inconsistency" in the warnings returned:
- past tense for deprecated function: "[..] **was** deprecated in [..]"
- present tense for deprecated argument: "[..] **is** deprecated as of [..]"

Shouldn't be always the same tense?

See reprex, where lifecycle 1.0.4 and R 4.4.1 has been used (Windows OS). Thanks in advance.

``` r
library(lifecycle)
a <- function(x) {
  lifecycle::deprecate_warn(when = "1.0.0",
                            what = "a()",
                            with = "b()",
                            always = TRUE
  )
  lifecycle::deprecate_warn(
    when = "1.0.0",
    what = "a(x)",
    with = "b(y)",
    always = TRUE
  )
}

# Run the function - returns the warnings
a(x = 1)
#> Warning: `a()` was deprecated in <NA> 1.0.0.
#> ℹ Please use `b()` instead.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
#> generated.
#> Warning: The `x` argument of `a()` is deprecated as of <NA> 1.0.0.
#> ℹ Please use the `y` argument of `b()` instead.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
```

title: Feature request: control lifecycle_verbosity via an environment variable
description:
Hi,

On build systems like the [Bioconductor build system](https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/3.17/bioc-LATEST/), we try hard to produce results that are reproducible by the package developers. 

However, the default behavior of things like `lifecycle::deprecate_soft()`, where the warning is issued once every 8 hours, hurts reproducibility: developers see warnings on their machines that they don't see on the daily build report.

So ideally, when code is run in the context of the daily builds, we'd want to issue those warnings every time, by setting global option `lifecycle_verbosity` to ` "warning"`, as instructed [here](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/reference/verbosity.html).

OTOH we also want to make it easy for the developers to use the same settings that we use on the build machines. The way we do this is by defining a bunch of environment variables in an Renviron file that we use on the build machines and share with the developers. The individual package-level reports contain a link to this Renviron file with instructions within the file of how to use it locally. See for example the "use the following settings" link on the package-level report for **BiocGenerics** [here](https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/3.17/bioc-LATEST/BiocGenerics).

Can the verbosity of deprecation signals be controlled via an environment variable? If not, is this something that you would consider adding?

Thanks,
H.

title: Inaccurate error message in lifecycle::deprecate_soft() and lifecycle::deprecate_warn()
description:
While I was playing around with `lifecycle::deprecate_soft()` before opening issue #150, I ran into the following:
```R
library(lifecycle)

options(lifecycle_verbosity="warning")

lifecycle::deprecate_soft(when="1.0.0", what="foo()")
# Warning message:
# `foo()` was deprecated in <NA> 1.0.0.
# Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
# generated. 
```
All good.

But then:
```R
lifecycle::deprecate_soft(when="1.0.0", what="foo()", with="bar")

# ! `what` must have function call syntax.

#   # Good:
#   deprecate_soft("bar()")
# 
#   # Bad:
#   deprecate_soft("bar")
# Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
```
Error should be "! \`**with**\` must have function call syntax" instead of "! \`**what**\` must have function call syntax".

`lifecycle::deprecate_warn()` has the same problem.

Best,

title: Capture deprecated_warn() conditions and resignal?
description:
Hello. Is there a mechanism available for capturing `lifecycle_stage` conditions signaled by `deprecated_warn()` and friends, such that one can re-signal them later as if they were not intercepted?

For example, consider:

```r
> lifecycle::deprecate_warn("1.0.0", "foo()", "bar()", always = TRUE)
Warning message:
`foo()` was deprecated in <NA> 1.0.0.
Please use `bar()` instead.
```

If we attempt to capture condition this, we get:

```r
> cond <- tryCatch(lifecycle::deprecate_warn("1.0.0", "foo()", "bar()", always = TRUE), condition = identity)

List of 8
```

This condition is not a `warning` condition, so using `signalCondition(cond)` will not generate the intended warning.

I understand that **lifecycle** uses another internal layer of condition handlers;

https://github.com/r-lib/lifecycle/blob/0a6860af815500c51697780464af19c0f389d2f6/R/deprecate.R#L252-L256

that comes into play. (I haven't tracked down the full call stack in the code, but some tracing/debugging led me to this piece of code.)

Is there a way to capture-and-resignal what `deprecate_warn()` and friends produces?

PS. My use case is to capture them in `future::future()`, possibly being resolved in another R process, and then relay them in the main R session as if they were produced there.

title: More flexible syntax for warning messages
description:
The challenge is to have a flexible UI that still makes it easy to supply the metadata stored in the warning conditions, that is package, function name, and argument name.

One way to go about this is to allow a length-2 vector whose first element defines the metadata, and the second specifies a warning message.

```r
deprecate_warn(
  "1.0.0",
  c("pkg::foo(bar)", message = "Supplying `bar = \"none\"` is deprecated.")
)
#> Warning message:
#> Supplying `bar = "none"` is deprecated.
```

We could use `...` as a placeholder that lifecycle could fill in with generated contents.

```r
deprecate_warn(
  "1.0.0",
  c("pkg::foo(bar)", message = "Supplying `bar = \"none\"`...")
)
#> Warning message:
#> Supplying `bar = "none"` is deprecated as of pkg 1.0.0.

deprecate_warn(
  "1.0.0",
  c("pkg::foo(bar)", message = "... can no longer be \"none\"...")
)
#> Warning message:
#> The `bar` argument of `foo()` can no longer be "none" as of pkg 1.0.0.
```

The `with` argument would also allow a `message` field:

```r
deprecate_warn(
  "1.0.0",
  what = c("pkg::foo(bar)", message = "Supplying `bar = \"none\"`..."),
  with = c(message = "Please use `bar = NULL` instead.")
)
#> Warning message:
#> Supplying `bar = "none"` is deprecated as of pkg 1.0.0.
#> Please use `bar = NULL` instead.
```

I like that this leverages existing syntax for defining a deprecation message + metadata.

What do you think @hadley?

title: Lifecycle API
description:
## Deprecating functions

Deprecation without replacement:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo")
#> `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0
```

Deprecation with replacement

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo", "bar")
#> `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0.
#> Please use `bar()` instead.
```

Just specify the namespace when replacement is in another package:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo", "otherpackage::bar")
#> `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0.
#> Please use `otherpackage::bar()` instead.
```

The package of the deprecated function is inferred from the caller env, but could also be specified manually if needed:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "otherpackage::foo")
#> `foo()` is deprecated as of otherpackage 0.3.0.
```

It is encouraged to provide details about the replacement:

```r
details <- "

  # Before:
  foo()

  # After:
  bar()
"

warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo", "bar", details)
#> `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0.
#> Please use `bar()` instead.
#>
#>   # Before:
#>   foo()
#>
#>   # After:
#>   bar()
```

## Deprecating arguments

Specify an argument:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo@bar")
#> The argument `bar` of `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0
```

The replacement can be a function:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo@bar", "quux")
#> The argument `bar` of `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0.
#> Please use `quux()` instead.
```

Or an argument:

```r
warn_deprecated("0.3.0", "foo@bar", "otherpackage::quux@baz")
#> The argument `bar` of `foo()` is deprecated as of rlang 0.3.0.
#> Please use the argument `baz` of `otherpackage::quux()` instead.
```
